verdicts.reason: A keeps the original reading order (headline, body, CTA, legal) but stretches it with oversized dead gaps between each block, and the book now sits loose on the top edge of the circle instead of inside it. B puts the CTA first, above the book and headline. Its body line runs across the circle, and the bottom third of the canvas is empty.

Both put the CTA above the headline. In A the CTA is jammed against '2 for 1', the body line runs almost to the right edge, and the book sits awkwardly on the circle's rim. B has the same CTA-first order, with the book between CTA and headline. Its CTA left edge (~75px) doesn't line up with the text column (~30px), and the bottom is empty.

A keeps the correct hierarchy and order but has loose, uneven vertical gaps, and the book is detached from its circle. B's two-column book/text split suits the square better. But the CTA is shrunk to a tiny pill in the top-right corner above the headline, the body and legal text sit on the circle with reduced contrast, and the bottom ~40% is empty.

A has a strong headline and a sensible two-column layout with a large book. But the CTA is a tiny pill above the headline, the copy overlaps the circle, and the lower half is dead space. B leads with the CTA jammed directly above the headline, the body line nearly hits the right edge, and the book hangs over the circle's rim, with an empty bottom.
